headline: Disabling Google AI Overviews can completely fix your search results
summary: Google's AI Overviews can still hallucinate and require verification, making traditional blue links more efficient. Learn simple methods to remove them from your search results.
details: Google's AI Overviews, despite improvements, still present challenges for users. The need to verify every fact due to potential hallucinations or incorrect sources makes the feature less efficient for many. Users often find it quicker to bypass the AI summaries altogether.

Google does not offer a straightforward toggle to disable AI Overviews within Chrome or the Google app. This suggests an intent to keep the feature prominent, requiring users to seek alternative methods for removal.

On desktop, one method is to use the "Web" filter found under the "More" tab. This removes AI Overviews but also strips out all other filters like videos, images, news, and shopping suggestions, leaving only traditional blue links.

A more flexible desktop solution involves setting up a custom search engine. By directing searches through a service like Udm14, users can automatically apply a filter that removes AI Overviews while retaining other search categories. This can be assigned a quick shortcut like "gg" for ease of use.

For mobile users, the most effective method is to add the " -ai " prefix before each search query. This removes AI Overviews while keeping other filters intact, though it requires manual entry for every search as mobile Chrome does not support custom search engines.

Extensions are generally not recommended as they often break and only hide AI Overviews rather than preventing them from loading, which might not reduce search costs. The manual methods offer more control and reliability.

Ultimately, understanding how to fine-tune Google Search queries with prefixes like " -ai " is a valuable skill. While AI Overviews have some utility, many prefer the directness of traditional search results, and these methods provide that control.

headline: Google destroys 1,300 acres of Finnish forest for AI data centers, wolves enter villages
summary: Google's unauthorized clearing of over 1,300 acres of forest in Finland for AI data centers has led to wolves and other wild animals encroaching on local villages, sparking safety concerns and environmental outrage.
details: Google's Finland country manager has apologized for unauthorized forest clearings near Muhos, turning 816 acres into mud. Work on roughly 500 more acres, 55 miles southeast of Otanmäki, has also been ordered to cease, bringing the total affected area to over 1,300 acres for new AI data centers.

The destruction has caused wolves, who previously lived in these forests, to roam into neighboring villages. Local families report wolves and other wild animals entering countryside areas, raising serious human safety concerns.

Local anger continues to simmer over Google's apparent disregard for regulations in its rush to build AI data centers. Residents also complain about construction noise, streams turning brown, and rare birds being displaced.

The Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) has ordered Google to stop development near Muhos and Otanmäki due to unprecedented policy flouting. Google has stated it will fully comply with LVV's requests and maintain an open dialogue.
Finland is not isolated in these concerns; similar environmental issues related to AI data center development have been reported across the U.S. and other countries.
